transcript:
Meeting header: Date: 2028-10-28 15:30 UTC | Duration: 63 minutes | Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Lydia Chen (Redwood SE), Marco Reyes (CTO - ApexFusion), Nina Patel (Head Cloud Ops), Tom Li (BizDev), Jae Park (Solutions Architect)

Summary: Quick discovery to map technical integration points for listing Redwood as a managed inference option in ApexFusion's GPU marketplace and to explore a channel agreement. We covered deployment patterns, security pre-reqs, benchmarking, and go-to-market responsibilities.

00:00 Samir (Redwood): Hey everyone thanks for taking the time. quick intros from our side, I'm Samir AE, with Lydia our SE who will drive the tech side.
00:14 Marco (ApexFusion): Hi all, Marco here. we run platform and infra, also curious about how you want to model the marketplace listing.
00:25 Lydia (Redwood): Hi, Lydia. we'll be honest upfront — there are a couple of ways to integrate: 1) simple managed listing where we operate endpoints and you resell; 2) an onramp where you surface our dedicated offering inside your marketplace and customers can provision capacity; 3) an OEM / white-label package for deeper reseller agreements.
00:48 Nina (ApexFusion): okay, can you say quick pros/cons? especially around customer data residency and VPCs.
00:57 Lydia (Redwood): Sure. managed listing = fastest time to market, Redwood-hosted, you get revenue share, limited VPC support (we can offer private deployment plans). dedicated/onramp = customers can spin up dedicated capacity in their region, supports VPC peering, KMS integration, and specific latency SLAs. OEM gets you control but longer engineering lift.
01:20 Tom (ApexFusion): what's the typical revenue split? and do you support per-subscription vs usage billing?
01:28 Samir (Redwood): We do both — marketplace usually gets a revenue share % on usage and reserved capacity deals can be custom. we'll share the partner pricing spreadsheet after this call.
01:40 Marco (ApexFusion): Technical question — kernel selection and quantization compatibility. Our customers run mixed workloads, some want 8-bit quant, some FP16. how brittle is your runtime?
01:55 Lydia (Redwood): Our runtime is flexible; we select kernels based on model arch and sequence lengths, but there are edge cases. we run a quick compatibility matrix during onboarding. note: sometimes our docs say k v cache as "k-v cash" in earlier drafts, so ignore typos, but the KV cache and prefix caching are central to throughput.
02:18 Jae (ApexFusion): Are there specific NVIDIA driver versions or cuda requirements? we operate several GPU families.
02:26 Lydia (Redwood): We support Ampere and Hopper stacks; recommended drivers are X.Y and Z.Z for best perf. we'll include a compatibility matrix. we also support CPU-only infer for small models but with big perf hit.
02:40 Nina (ApexFusion): Security — SOC 2, SSO, KMS. customers will ask.
02:46 Samir (Redwood): We're SOC 2 Type II certified, SAML SSO and RBAC supported, KMS/HSM integrations for Private. we'll send the SOC 2 report and our private deployment checklist.
03:05 Marco (ApexFusion): For marketplace — do you want to be a managed vendor where we just surface an API key, or do you want deeper integration with our provisioning flow?
03:18 Samir (Redwood): Preference toward a managed listing initially, but we're open to deeper provisioning for larger customers. starting managed reduces integration friction.
03:30 Tom (ApexFusion): Ok makes sense. let's talk pilot. what would a 6-week pilot look like?
03:37 Lydia (Redwood): Week 0: exchange test artifacts and access. Week 1–2: run kernel and latency benchmarks on your test cluster; Week 3–4: customer-like load tests and regression checks; Week 5–6: finalize SLOs and document economics.
03:56 Marco (ApexFusion): On the cluster — we can give a sandbox with one A100/80GB and a Hopper test node. do you need container images?
04:06 Lydia (Redwood): Yes we prefer a model container and a networked node. provide SSH + limited service account or we can run a remote agent. we'll create test scripts (open-source-ish) to run perf runs.
04:19 Samir (Redwood): we'll also need sample prompts and a small eval set for quality checks so caching doesn't mask quality regressions.
04:30 Jae (ApexFusion): licensing — are there restrictions on models you host? customers often bring third-party models.
04:38 Lydia (Redwood): We support customer models and public model catalog; licensing depends on the model. for private deployments customers can pin versions.
04:50 Marco (ApexFusion): Pricing control — can marketplace show an estimated cost per 1k tokens?
04:56 Samir (Redwood): Yes we can provide per-token cost breakdowns and latency estimates per model. Redwood Console gives token-level cost and latency. we'll provide a sample screenshot and API hooks.
05:10 Tom (ApexFusion): Integration ops — what about billing reconciliation, metering, and attribution for channel revenue splits?
05:20 Samir (Redwood): We provide metering logs with per-customer attribution, usage exports and can integrate with your billing via webhooks or flat exports.
05:32 Nina (ApexFusion): Data residency — if a customer requires EU-only, can you pin region?
05:39 Lydia (Redwood): Yes for Dedicated/Private we can pin region and ensure data stays in-region; for hosted listings we'll need to map to region endpoints.
05:52 Marco (ApexFusion): Any gotchas you've seen with partners previously?
06:00 Samir (Redwood): Biggest friction is expected SLAs vs actual peak throttling — we mitigate with routing/fallbacks and burst capacity, but it's important to scope expected traffic patterns early. also sometimes partners assume full feature parity across model variants which isn't always true.
06:20 Jae (ApexFusion): Benchmarks — can you run both latency p50/p95 and token throughput? we want both.
06:28 Lydia (Redwood): Yes. we'll run p50/p95 and tail latency, token/sec with different sequence lengths and batching configs. plan to test cold vs hot cache scenarios.
06:42 Tom (ApexFusion): Marketing — co-marketing and case studies?
06:48 Samir (Redwood): We do joint webinars and customer case studies for pilots that convert. typical ask is a 3–6 month exclusivity window per vertical for GTM support.
06:59 Marco (ApexFusion): About support SLAs — do you offer 24/7 on dedicated?
07:05 Lydia (Redwood): Yes for Dedicated we can offer enterprise support tiers, 24/7 on-call for sev1, with escalation paths.
07:16 Nina (ApexFusion): Can you handle private deployments inside customer's VPC with KMS? some regulated customers mandate that.
07:23 Lydia (Redwood): Absolutely. Private includes VPC and KMS/HSM integration; audit logs and access controls are available.
07:33 Samir (Redwood): Ok quick recap, we'll: send partner deck + pricing, SOC2, private deployment checklist. Lydia will draft the benchmark plan. ApexFusion will provide test cluster access and sample model container.
07:50 Marco (ApexFusion): sounds good. any blockers from our side? we need to review commercial terms and legal review but that's standard.
07:59 Tom (ApexFusion): timeline — if we start bench wk of Nov 6 we can aim for a joint pilot announcement in late December?
08:06 Samir (Redwood): That seems reasonable. follow-up meeting in 2 weeks to agree SOW.
08:12 Recording note: some transcription errors — names and acronyms may be slightly off.

(Several sections of the call contained live-screen sharing demos of the Redwood Console and the ApexFusion marketplace UI — screenshots and the partner pricing spreadsheet referenced in chat)

58:30 Samir (Redwood): Alright thanks everyone we'll circle back with materials.
58:36 Marco (ApexFusion): Thanks all.
58:39 Tom (ApexFusion): Appreciate it.
58:42 Lydia (Redwood): Bye.

End of transcript.
